source.title: Self-Referenced Deep Learning
source.authors: Xu Lan; Xiatian Zhu; S. Gong

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports effects of its self-distillation training method on accuracy and local-minimum width, but does not test any listed claim version: it has no random-label capacity experiment, width sweep, architecture comparison, optimizer or batch-size comparison, dropout test, magnitude-aware sharpness comparison, or memorized-example removal.
record.gate_note: The reported SRDL results compare a new two-stage self-distillation recipe with vanilla training and knowledge distillation. They do not test whether networks that fit random labels generalize, or any listed version. Rows record the paper's own accuracy and perturbation-width results as findings about generalization outside the mapped versions.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates self-distillation, not any listed version. Its closest result to V7 compares two solutions using absolute, unscaled parameter perturbations and cross-entropy loss; it does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness, train–test gaps, or rankings against norm and margin measures. Fixed batch sizes and SGD settings provide no tests of V4 or V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that SRDL improves tested classification and re-identification performance over vanilla training with little extra computational cost, and report a wider local minimum in their perturbation analysis. Their comparison with conventional distillation is conditional: SRDL consistently beats the ResNet-110 teacher configuration, but trails the WRN-28-10 teacher configuration on CIFAR100 and Tiny ImageNet.
record.recipe_differences: Two-stage self-distillation training with extracted intermediate class probabilities, a stage-complete learning-rate schedule, and random restart; not a test of the listed claim recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: On CIFAR100 ResNet-32, stage-complete versus stage-incomplete scheduling and second-stage random restart change reported accuracy; ensemble choice changes accuracy and deployment cost.

fits_no_version.finding: SRDL improves held-out classification and person re-identification performance over vanilla training in the tested configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Two-stage self-distillation can improve held-out performance at the same training epoch budget with marginal knowledge-extraction cost.

fits_no_version.finding: SRDL outperforms ResNet-110-teacher distillation on all three classification datasets, but beats WRN-28-10-teacher distillation only on CIFAR10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-distillation's accuracy relative to conventional distillation depends on teacher and dataset, while avoiding separate teacher-training cost.

fits_no_version.finding: Stage-complete scheduling and random restart improve SRDL accuracy; ensembling adds accuracy and doubles deployment cost.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SRDL performance depends on its schedule, restart, and ensemble choices.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report a wider local minimum for SRDL than vanilla training under absolute parameter perturbations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested SRDL ResNet-32 solution is more robust to the paper's unscaled perturbations than its vanilla counterpart.

record.problems: No random-label memorization or train-test gap experiment. Classification results are reported as averages of 5 independent runs but no variance or confidence interval is supplied. Fig. 4 gives perturbation curves without numerical width values. Table 3 is flattened in the supplied text, preventing reliable assignment of some displayed multi-query values.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-version result rows identified. Table 3 multi-query ResNet-50 mAP could not be assigned reliably from the flattened table and is retained as an indeterminate row rather than reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting capacity and its coexistence with natural-label held-out generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the role of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including tuning, weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes that recover performance.
Dropout effects across training-set sizes, strengths, and augmentation or weight-decay settings.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus train–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparison with norm and margin measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain linked to none. Their cannot_determine states indicate that they cannot establish a listed version, not that their reported performance differences are unreadable. Table 3's ResNet-50 entries are recoverable from the supplied sequence and the matching gain entries. No omitted result bears on a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and interaction with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with train-test gaps.
Effect of removing memorized training examples.
